AWPTCM-T33373.objective:
• Devices roaming to another port on the same authenticator retain authenticated state and communicate successfully without triggering re-authentication, for MAC authentication and Web authentication modes.
  • Roaming authentication does not extend to dot1x-authenticated sessions: a supplicant moving ports under dot1x is confirmed to require full re-authentication rather than roaming, distinguishing dot1x from MAC/Web authentication behaviour.
  • ARP resolution for a roamed device is correctly re-established on the new port without requiring supplicant re-authentication, with no stale ARP entries left against the original port.
  • When the supplicant's attached interface is link-downed rather than roamed, authentication state is cleared and re-authentication is executed on reconnection, rather than being treated as a roam.
  • Repeated roaming activity sustained overnight remains stable: authentication and communication continue to succeed on each roam, with no errors and no memory leak observed over the duration.
  • Authentication and roaming events (successful roams, denied dot1x roams, link-down triggered re-authentications) are observable and distinguishable in device logs/status output for verification and troubleshooting.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Set up authenticator with two ports available for roaming and a supplicant configured for MAC authentication. Authenticate the supplicant on Port A and confirm authenticated state.

Move the MAC-authenticated supplicant's physical connection from Port A to Port B on the same authenticator. Verify the device retains its authenticated state and does not trigger a new authentication attempt.
steps.expectedResult: Session shows as roamed/retained, not re-authenticated.

steps.description: Test with traffic (e.g. ping) from the roamed MAC-authenticated device to confirm it communicates successfully on the new port.
Repeat the roam using a Web-authenticated supplicant: authenticate on Port A, then move to Port B on the same authenticator. Verify authenticated state is retained without re-authentication.
Test with traffic from the roamed Web-authenticated device to confirm successful communication on the new port.
Set up a dot1x-authenticated supplicant on Port A and confirm authenticated state. Move the supplicant to Port B on the same authenticator.
Verify the dot1x supplicant is denied roaming treatment and is required to fully re-authenticate on the new port, distinguishing this behaviour from MAC/Web authentication roaming.
steps.expectedResult: Full 802.1X re-authentication occurs; roam is not permitted.

steps.description: Confirm ARP resolution for the roamed device is correctly re-established on the new port without requiring supplicant re-authentication.
Verify no stale ARP entry remains against the original port after the roam completes.
steps.expectedResult: ARP table shows entry only against the new port.

steps.description: Set the supplicant's attached interface to link-down (rather than physically roaming) and confirm authentication state is cleared as a result.
Reconnect the link and verify full re-authentication is executed on reconnection, confirming this is treated as a re-authentication event rather than a roam.
Test with sustained repeated roaming activity over an overnight period across MAC and Web authenticated sessions. Verify authentication and communication succeed on each roam throughout the duration.
steps.expectedResult: No failed roams or communication drops observed.

steps.description: Verify no errors are logged and no memory leak is observed on the authenticator over the course of the overnight roaming test.
steps.expectedResult: Memory utilisation stable; no error log entries.

steps.description: Verify device logs/status output distinctly record successful roam events (MAC/Web), denied dot1x roam attempts, and link-down triggered re-authentications for troubleshooting purposes.
steps.expectedResult: Each event type is separately identifiable in logs/status output.
